subject: RFP: Dedicated GPU mix & throughput — workshop summary and workbook
messages:
From: Jake Reynolds <j.reynolds@orion-analytics.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orion-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFP — Dedicated GPU sizing: initial questionnaire

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our RFP. We're consolidating inference for a set of internal AI services and need Redwood's input on dedicated capacity sizing. Attached is the high-level RFP; our procurement team is primarily focused on predictable monthly cost and reservation commitments.

High-level asks:
- Typical GPU mix you recommend for mixed workloads (Llama2-70B-like and LLM-slim 7B variants)
- Target RPS/throughput per GPU at avg sequence length 512 and p50/p95 latencies
- Reservation model options for burst and baseline (committed vs. burst pool)
- Any minimum contract term that materially changes unit pricing

We'd like a short workshop this week to review a sizing workbook. Can you send the workbook and a preliminary recommendation before the call?

Thanks,
Jake
Jake Reynolds
Director, AI Infrastructure
Orion Analytics

[attachment: orion_rfp_summary_20261216.pdf]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-16T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP — Dedicated GPU sizing: initial questionnaire

Jake —

Appreciate the RFP and the clear ask. We've put together a first-pass Dedicated Sizing Workbook and a short assumptions PDF to bring to the workshop. I've attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_ORION_v1.xlsx (editable), throughput-assumptions-and-costs.pdf, and a CSV of our recommended GPU profiles.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Recommended GPU mix: 60% q8_4xA800-like (cost-efficient 4x partitions), 30% A100-80GB or equivalent for latency-sensitive heavy tokens, 10% reserved NVidia H100 nodes for peak long-context generation jobs.
- Expected throughput (per physical GPU): 7B-class models: ~1200 requests/hour at avg seq 512 (batching 8, p50 latency ~60ms).
  70B-class: ~110 requests/hour at avg seq 512 (batching 4, p50 latency ~220ms).
- Reservation model: baseline committed pool sized to meet your p99 throughput target for steady-state, plus shared burst pool for 2–4x short-term bursts. Burst pricing is higher but preserves baseline SLAs.
- Pricing: 12-month commitments reduce unit cost ~18% vs month-to-month; 36-month adds further ~6%.

Marissa (cc'd) will lead the workshop and walk through the workbook; Priyom will validate throughput assumptions against your sample traces if you can share them.

Proposed workshop windows: 2026-12-17 10:00–11:00 PT or 2026-12-18 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

[attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_ORION_v1.xlsx, throughput-assumptions-and-costs.pdf, gpu_profile_recommendations_2026.csv]

Kimberly / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook. A couple of clarifying items before the workshop so we can prep traces:  
1) The numbers for 70B-class look optimistic for our 1k token gen jobs. Can you clarify the batching assumptions (batch size, concurrency) used to estimate 110 reqs/hour?
2) For the 'shared burst pool' — do burst nodes use the same kernel/quantization profile as baseline? Any fallbacks to smaller models during severe load?
3) Can you include an example cost comparison in the workbook for 12 vs 36 months for our baseline profile (baseline = 250 concurrent steady RPS at seq512)?

We'll share a 48-hour trace (anonymized) just prior to the workshop. Workshop slot 2026-12-17 10:00 PT works for us.

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@orion-analytics.com>, Jake Reynolds <j.reynolds@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-17T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP — Dedicated GPU sizing: initial questionnaire (detailed baking of assumptions)

Dan / Jake —

Thanks for the trace and good questions. Below are the explicit assumptions used to derive the per-GPU throughput estimates; we'll slot these into the workbook as a labeled assumptions sheet for auditability.

Assumptions (short):
- Model families: 7B (quantized int8/q4_variant) and 70B (q8_4x mixed-precision recommended).
- Batching: nominal batching strategy is micro-batch (up to 8 for 7B when latency target <=200ms) and greedy batching for throughput windows; for 70B we assume batch sizes 2–4 depending on concurrency.
- Concurrency: baseline tests used 16 concurrent worker threads per physical GPU for 7B, and 6–8 for 70B.
- Sequence length profile: avg 512 tokens; 95th percentile 1024 tokens for synthetic worst-case.
- Kernel selection: A800-like partitioned kernels for cost efficiency in mixed workloads; A100/H100 recommended for long-context and lower p95.

Concrete numbers (from lab profiles; per physical GPU):
- 7B quantized (q4-like): 1,350 requests / hour @ avg512, p50 ~55ms, p95 ~180ms (batch 6–8, concurrency 16).
- 70B q8_4x: 95–130 requests / hour @ avg512 depending on prompt composition, p50 200–260ms, p95 600–900ms (batch 2–4, concurrency 6).

Reservation model notes:
- Baseline committed pool: size to cover p95 of typical daily traffic for mission-critical services; baseline priced at committed rate.
- Burst pool: ephemeral capacity run on a higher-price tier (same kernels but scraped of reserved discounts) — can also be configured to fallback to smaller model variants automatically if latency becomes critical. We recommend a policy: baseline covers 70% of observed p95; burst pool covers +150% of baseline for short intervals.

12 vs 36 month economics:
- We added a sample sheet in the workbook that models baseline sizes, expected token volumes, and per-GPU effective hourly costs. The workbook includes toggles for commitment length (1, 12, 36 months) and for GPU mix sensitivity.

Attached: updated workbook tab 'ASSUMPTIONS_v2' and gpu_profile_recommendations_2026.csv (includes kernel hints and quantization targets).

We'll review these line-by-line in the workshop at 10:00 PT. If you want, Priyom can run your redacted trace through our sizing script live.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

[attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_ORION_v1.xlsx (updated), gpu_profile_recommendations_2026.csv, throughput-assumptions-and-costs.pdf]

Subject: Re: RFP — Dedicated GPU sizing: workshop recap and next steps

Marissa / Kimberly —

Good workshop — thanks for walking through the workbook and running the trace. Notes / next steps:  
- Orion accepts the recommended baseline/burst split for the initial pilot: baseline = 80 A800-partition equivalents (as modeled) + 10 A100-80GB for lower latency endpoints.
- Please provide a formal cost breakdown for 12 and 36 month commitments by EOD Wednesday (include effective hourly unit cost and assumptions).
- We want an automated fallback policy in the deployment spec that routes to 7B variants when 70B p95 > 700ms (we'll share our SLOs).
- Procurement requests standard SLA language and a short addendum describing data retention on Dedicated servers.

Action owners: Redwood to send formal cost worksheet + SLA addendum (Kimberly), Redwood engineering to provide fallback policy template (Marissa), Orion to share final SLOs and a confirmation of pilot start date (Jake/Dan).

We'll loop legal after cost numbers. Thanks again.

Dan
Principal SRE, Orion Analytics
